qualification.reason: The document is a Request for Quotations (RFQ) issued by NYS Office of General Services for an Aggregate Hardware Buy, with clear procurement intent, submission deadlines, evaluation criteria, and contract terms.

quotes.quote: RFQ Title Aggregate Hardware Buy 23-01 RFQ Number 23-01
Request for Quotations 23-01

OGS is seeking competitive quotes from Contract holders of the OGS Group 73600 Award 22802 Information Technology Umbrella Contract – Manufacturer Based (Statewide) (“Manufacturer Umbrella Contract”) for the Lot(s) indicated below.
BASIS FOR AWARD Highest Total Financial Score meeting specified Technical Requirements and Mandatory Pass/Fail Requirements for each Standard Configuration and associated Required Products.

OGS is releasing this Request for Quotes (RFQ) for Aggregate Hardware Buy 23-01 (“RFQ 23-01”).  The purpose of RFQ 23-01 is to establish an award for each Configuration as set forth in Attachment A - Technical Response.

Quotes and pricing submitted in response to RFQ 23-01 must remain open and valid for at least 120 calendar days from the date that RFQ Submissions are due, unless the time for making an award is extended by mutual consent of OGS and the Contractor.

findings.title: Purchase Order Receipt Notification: 5 Calendar Days
findings.fact: The Contractor must provide a Purchase Order receipt notification to the Authorized User within five (5) calendar days of receipt of a Purchase Order.

quotes.quote: The Contractor must provide a Purchase Order receipt notification to the Authorized User within five (5) calendar days of receipt of a Purchase Order.

findings.title: Advanced Shipping Notice: 14 Calendar Days Prior to Delivery
findings.fact: An Advanced Shipping Notice must be provided to Authorized Users upon request fourteen (14) calendar days prior to delivery.

quotes.quote: An Advanced Shipping Notice must be provided to Authorized Users upon request fourteen (14) calendar days prior to delivery.

findings.title: Quarterly Sales Reports Due One Month After Quarter End
findings.fact: Sales reports are due to OGS one (1) month directly following the end of each quarter.

quotes.quote: Sales reports are due to OGS one (1) month directly following the end of each quarter.

findings.title: EOL Notice for Additional Products: 60 Calendar Days
findings.fact: OGS must receive no less than 60 calendar days notice for EOL Additional Products.

quotes.quote: OGS must receive no less than 60 calendar days notice for EOL Additional Products.

findings.title: EOL Notice for Replacement Products: 60 Calendar Days
findings.fact: OGS must receive no less than 60 calendar days notice from Contractor for EOL Products, in order for OGS to process modifications for Product substitutions in a timely manner.

quotes.quote: OGS must receive no less than 60 calendar days notice from Contractor for EOL Products, in order for OGS to process modifications for Product substitutions in a timely manner.

findings.title: EOL Notice for Standard Configuration: 60 Calendar Days Prior
findings.fact: OGS must receive notification no less than 60 calendar days prior to the EOL of an awarded Standard Configuration model or the date that the awarded Standard Configuration becomes unavailable for purchase.

quotes.quote: OGS must receive notification no less than 60 calendar days prior to the EOL of an awarded Standard Configuration model or the date that the awarded Standard Configuration becomes unavailable for purchase.

findings.title: Substitute Standard Configuration Submission: 30 Calendar Days Prior to EOL
findings.fact: No less than 30 calendar days prior to the EOL of the awarded Standard Configuration or the date that the awarded Standard Configuration has become unavailable for purchase by Authorized Users, a substitute Standard Configuration with specifications that meet or exceed the specifications of the original offered Standard Configuration must be submitted for OGS approval.

quotes.quote: No less than 30 calendar days prior to the EOL of the awarded Standard Configuration or the date that the awarded Standard Configuration has become unavailable for purchase by Authorized Users, a substitute Standard Configuration with specifications that meet or exceed the specifications of the original offered Standard Configuration must be submitted for OGS approval by completing the modification process outlined in Appendix 2 – Agreement Price List Modification Procedures.

findings.title: Customized Factory Imaging Test Unit: 5 Business Days
findings.fact: If an Authorized User requires customized factory imaging, the Contractor shall provide a test unit with the customized image within five (5) business days of receiving the Authorized User’s image.

quotes.quote: If an Authorized User requires customized factory imaging, the Contractor shall provide a test unit with the customized image within five (5) business days of receiving the Authorized User’s image.

findings.title: Delivery of Imaged Units: 30 Calendar Days from Approval
findings.fact: The Contractor must deliver the remainder of the imaged units ordered by the Authorized User, within 30 calendar days from the date of Authorized User’s written approval of the test unit.

quotes.quote: The Contractor must deliver the remainder of the imaged units ordered by the Authorized User, within 30 calendar days from the date of Authorized User’s written approval of the test unit.

findings.title: Customer Service Response: 24 Hours
findings.fact: Inquiries shall be responded to within twenty-four (24) hours.

quotes.quote: Inquiries shall be responded to within twenty-four (24) hours.

findings.title: Sales Report Backup Documentation: 15 Business Days
findings.fact: If requested by OGS, Contractor shall provide backup documentation of all quarterly sales reports to support a sales and fiscal audit. These records will be made available on request, no more than 15 business days after request.

quotes.quote: If requested by OGS, Contractor shall provide backup documentation of all quarterly sales reports to support a sales and fiscal audit. These records will be made available on request, no more than 15 business days after request, in a searchable electronic format as specified by OGS.

findings.title: Fiscal Audit Notice: 15 Business Days
findings.fact: Audits shall be conducted during regular business hours, upon not less than 15 business days prior written notice.

quotes.quote: Audits shall be conducted during regular business hours, upon not less than 15 business days prior written notice.

findings.title: Stage 1 Administrative Review
findings.fact: Stage 1 reviews completeness of Attachment A, Attachment D, and Manufacturer Information page. Alterations to documents are prohibited and may result in rejection.

quotes.quote: The submitted Attachment A – Technical Response, Attachment D – Issue Escalation Plan, and the Manufacturer Information page (last page of this document) will be reviewed for completeness.  The addition or deletion of worksheets, columns, unlocking the document, rewriting formulas, or similar alterations to any document is prohibited. OGS reserves the right to reject any RFQ Submission or portion(s) thereof determined to have been altered/modified by the Contractor from the original format. Failure to provide fully completed documents may result in rejection of the RFQ Submission without further review.

findings.title: OGS Reserved Right to Modify Specifications Prior to Financial Evaluation
findings.fact: OGS may modify a specification within the Standard Configuration or Required Product categories prior to the Financial Evaluation.

quotes.quote: Modify a specification within the Standard Configuration or Required Product categories in Attachment A – Technical Response or Attachment C – Financial Response prior to the Financial Evaluation, upon written notice to Contractors that have submitted a quote.

findings.title: Additional Products Discount Application
findings.fact: The same discount percentages bid for Required Product categories apply to Additional Products in their respective categories.

quotes.quote: Contractors shall provide the same awarded discount percentages that applied to the three (3) Required Product categories (Warranty and Services, Components, and Peripherals), to the Additional Products in their respective categories.

findings.title: Discount Percentage Formatting
findings.fact: Discount percentage values must not exceed two decimal places and cannot be expressed as a range.

quotes.quote: All Discount percentage values shall not exceed two decimal places (for example: 20.25222% shall be rounded to nearest one hundredth 20.25%). OGS will round any discount percentage to the nearest hundredth if necessary. A Discount Percentage value cannot be expressed as a range (for example: 10%-20%, or “varies”).

findings.title: Warranty Obligations
findings.fact: Contractor must provide new replacement units for inoperable units within warranty, and provide warranty SKUs for docking stations and additional warranty years.

quotes.quote: If a unit becomes inoperable within the warranty window and cannot be repaired, a brand new unit shall be provided at no charge.
The Contractor is responsible for providing a warranty SKU(s) for docking stations listed as a Required Product or Additional Product on the price lists.
The Contractor is responsible for adding SKUs for additional warranty year options (e.g. 3 year, 4 year, 5 year) under Additional Products on Attachment A – Technical Response.

findings.title: Only Lot 2 Hardware Contractors Eligible
findings.fact: Only Contractors holding an award for Lot 2 – Hardware under the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract are eligible to bid; Resellers are not eligible and will be disqualified.
findings.business_implication: This RFQ is restricted to existing Lot 2 Hardware contract holders. Resellers or non-Lot 2 contractors cannot participate, and any bid from them will be rejected. This limits the competition to a specific group of pre-approved contractors.
findings.action_recommendation: Confirm that your company holds a Lot 2 Hardware award under the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract. If not, do not attempt to bid, as it will be disqualified. If you are a reseller, consider partnering with a Lot 2 contractor or exploring other opportunities.

quotes.quote: Quotes from Resellers will not be accepted. Contractors must have an award for Lot 2 to bid on this RFQ.

RFQ 23-01 is only being distributed to Contractors holding an award for Lot 2 – Hardware under the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract (“Contractors”). Quotes under RFQ 23-01 will only be accepted from Lot 2 Contractors on the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract; Resellers are not eligible to respond and any bids from a Reseller will be disqualified.

findings.title: Products Must Be on Manufacturer Umbrella Contract Price List
findings.fact: All proposed products must be on the Contractor's Manufacturer Umbrella Contract Lot 2 - Hardware price list at the time of the RFQ Submission due date.
findings.business_implication: All products offered in the bid, including standard configurations, required products, and additional products, must be listed on the contractor's approved Manufacturer Umbrella Contract price list. If any SKU is not on the list, the bid may be rejected or not proceed in evaluation.
findings.action_recommendation: Before the RFQ submission due date, verify that every SKU you intend to propose is on your approved Manufacturer Umbrella Contract price list. If any product is missing, initiate a contract modification request promptly, indicating it is for RFQ 23-01, and ensure it is approved before the deadline.

quotes.quote: All Products proposed as part of the Standard Configuration and Products proposed for Required Products, as well as any Additional Products, must be on the Contractor's Manufacturer Umbrella Contract Lot 2 - Hardware price list at the time of the RFQ Submission due date.
All proposed SKUs for Products offered must be on the Contractor’s approved Manufacturer Umbrella Contract price list prior to the RFQ Submission due date for RFQ 23-01.

findings.title: Bid Validity Period
findings.fact: Quotes and pricing must remain valid for at least 120 calendar days from the RFQ submission due date.
findings.business_implication: Your bid must remain open and valid for at least 120 days from the submission deadline. This means you must be prepared to honor your pricing and terms for that extended period, which could affect your cost assumptions and resource allocation.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that your pricing strategy accounts for the 120-day validity period. Consider potential market fluctuations and ensure your internal approvals allow for this extended commitment. Also, be aware that OGS may request an extension by mutual consent, so be prepared to negotiate if needed.

quotes.quote: Quotes and pricing submitted in response to RFQ 23-01 must remain open and valid for at least 120 calendar days from the date that RFQ Submissions are due, unless the time for making an award is extended by mutual consent of OGS and the Contractor.

findings.title: No Exceptions to Appendix A and Material Terms
findings.fact: OGS will not entertain exceptions to Appendix A (Standard Clauses) or material exceptions to the RFQ or Appendix B.
findings.business_implication: You must accept all terms in Appendix A (Standard Clauses for New York State Contracts) without exception. Additionally, you cannot propose material deviations from the RFQ or Appendix B (General Specifications). Any attempt to do so may render your bid non-responsive and lead to rejection.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully review Appendix A and Appendix B to ensure you can fully comply with all terms. Do not submit any exceptions or alternative terms for these sections. If you have concerns, raise them during the question period, but be prepared that OGS will not accept material changes.

quotes.quote: Contractor is advised that OGS will not entertain any exceptions to Appendix A (Standard Clauses for New York State Contracts). OGS will also not entertain exceptions to the RFQ or Appendix B (General Specifications) that are of a material and substantive nature.

findings.title: Eligibility restricted to Manufacturer Umbrella Contract holders
findings.fact: Only Contractors with an approved Manufacturer Umbrella Contract can participate in RFQ 23-01.
findings.business_implication: Participation is limited to contractors who already have an approved Manufacturer Umbrella Contract. This means you must have an existing contractual relationship with OGS under that umbrella contract to be eligible. Additional products must also be on your approved price list.
findings.action_recommendation: Verify that your company has an approved Manufacturer Umbrella Contract and that all proposed additional products are on your price list. If you are not a contract holder, you cannot bid. If you are, ensure your contract is active and in good standing.

quotes.quote: All Additional Products proposed by a Contractor on Attachment A – Technical Response and Attachment C – Financial Response must first be on Contractor’s approved Manufacturer Umbrella Contract price list.

The terms and conditions of the Contractor’s Manufacturer Umbrella Contract including any Amendments and the additional terms and conditions set forth in this RFQ 23-01, Section 7, Terms and Conditions govern any resulting award under RFQ 23-01.

findings.title: Exclusion of entities on US Customs and Border Patrol lists
findings.fact: OGS will not accept a bid from a Contractor or a Contractor Product that contains Products made by an entity on any of the lists maintained by the US Customs and Border Patrol.
findings.business_implication: Bidders must ensure that their products and components are not sourced from entities on the US CBP withhold release orders or findings lists, as non-compliance will result in bid rejection.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the CBP list and verify that all proposed products and their components are not from listed entities. If any product is affected, remove it from the bid or propose a compliant replacement.

quotes.quote: OGS will not accept a bid from a Contractor, or a Contractor Product that contains Products made by an entity on any of the lists maintained by the US Customs and Border Patrol at the link set out below.

findings.title: EPEAT certification required for desktops, laptops, and monitors
findings.fact: Desktops, laptops, and computer monitors must have EPEAT Gold certification at time of award, except Chromebooks which require EPEAT Silver.
findings.business_implication: Products must meet specific environmental certification standards to be eligible for award. Failure to meet these requirements could disqualify the bid.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure all proposed desktops, laptops, and monitors have EPEAT Gold certification, and Chromebooks have EPEAT Silver, at the time of award. Verify certifications and include proof in the bid.

quotes.quote: Desktops, laptops, and computer monitors provided under any resulting Agreement are required to have achieved a minimum certification of EPEAT Gold at the time of award with the exception of the three Chromebook Configurations (Chromebook Low, Chromebook with Touchscreen and Chromebook with Touchscreen – 14”). Chromebook Standard Configurations will be required to meet a minimum certification of EPEAT Silver at the time of award.

findings.title: Contractor must be a Manufacturer Umbrella Contract holder
findings.fact: The RFQ is open only to Contractors holding a Manufacturer Umbrella Contract under Group 73600 – Award 22802.
findings.business_implication: Only contractors with an existing Manufacturer Umbrella Contract are eligible to bid. Bidders without this contract will be disqualified.
findings.action_recommendation: Confirm that your company holds a valid Manufacturer Umbrella Contract under Group 73600 – Award 22802. If not, do not submit a bid, or consider partnering with an eligible contractor.

quotes.quote: Office of General Services Procurement Services Group 73600 – Award 22802 IT Umbrella Contract – Manufacturer Based (Statewide) RFQ 23-01 - Aggregate Hardware Buy - REVISED

findings.title: Delivery Deadline: 45 Calendar Days
findings.fact: The Contractor shall deliver the units ordered by an Authorized User within 45 calendar days of receipt of a Purchase Order, unless an extension is granted.
findings.business_implication: The contractor must be able to meet a 45-day delivery deadline for all orders. Failure to do so may result in penalties or loss of contract.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess your supply chain and logistics capabilities to ensure you can deliver within 45 days. If there are potential delays, plan for contingencies or request extensions as per the terms.

quotes.quote: The Contractor shall deliver the units ordered by an Authorized User within 45 calendar days of receipt of a Purchase Order, approved by OSC if applicable, unless either the Authorized User or OGS grants an extension of time as provided below.

findings.title: Basis for Award
findings.fact: Awards will be made to the responsive and responsible Contractor(s) with the highest Total Financial Score per Configuration that meets all specified technical requirements. The same Contractor can be awarded multiple Configurations.
findings.business_implication: The award is based on the highest financial score per configuration, so pricing is a critical factor. Bidders must offer competitive pricing to win.
findings.action_recommendation: Develop a competitive pricing strategy for each configuration you bid on, ensuring you meet all technical requirements. Consider aggressive discounts to improve your Total Financial Score.

quotes.quote: Awards will be made to the responsive and responsible Contractor(s) with the highest Total Financial Score per Configuration that meets all the specified technical requirements.  The same Contractor can be awarded multiple Configurations.

findings.title: Mandatory Offerings
findings.fact: For each configuration bid, bidders must offer all components within the standard configuration and all required products. Failure to complete all required fields may result in rejection.
findings.business_implication: Incomplete bids will be rejected without further review, risking loss of business opportunity and wasted effort.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure all required fields in Attachments A and C are fully completed for each configuration bid, and double-check for completeness before submission.

quotes.quote: FOR EACH CONFIGURATION BID, BIDDERS MUST OFFER ALL COMPONENTS WITHIN THE STANDARD CONFIGURATION AND  ALL REQUIRED PRODUCTS . Failure to complete all required fields in Attachment A – Technical Response or Attachment C – Financial Response may result in rejection of the RFQ Submission without further review.

findings.title: Stage 2 Technical Evaluation
findings.fact: Stage 2 compares Attachment A to Standard Configuration and Required Products requirements. All proposed SKUs must be on the Contractor's approved Manufacturer Umbrella Contract price list. Any configuration with a SKU not on the price list may not proceed further.
findings.business_implication: If any proposed SKU is not on the approved price list, the entire configuration may be disqualified, potentially eliminating the bidder from consideration for that configuration.
findings.action_recommendation: Verify that all SKUs proposed in Attachment A are included on the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract price list before submission. If any are missing, initiate contract modification requests promptly.

quotes.quote: Submitted Attachment A – Technical Response will be compared to Standard Configuration and Required Products requirements.  All proposed SKUs for proposed products offered in Attachment A – Technical Response must be on the Contractor’s approved Manufacturer Umbrella Contract price list. Any Configuration that contains a SKU that is not included on the Manufacturer’s Umbrella Contract price list may not proceed further in the evaluation process.

findings.title: Stage 3 Financial Evaluation
findings.fact: Only Contractors whose Standard Configuration specifications and Required Products pass review will proceed to evaluation of Attachment C – Financial Response. The proposed pricing on Attachment C will be used in the Financial Evaluation.
findings.business_implication: Financial evaluation is contingent on passing technical review; therefore, technical compliance is a prerequisite for pricing consideration.
findings.action_recommendation: Focus on ensuring technical compliance first, as financial evaluation will only occur for technically compliant configurations. Prepare Attachment C pricing in advance but be ready to adjust based on technical outcomes.

quotes.quote: Only Contractors whose Standard Configuration specifications and Required Products pass review, as determined by OGS, will proceed to the evaluation of Attachment C – Financial Response for those specific Configurations. For those Contractors who have been determined to have passed the Technical Evaluation, their Attachment A - Technical Response will be used to create the Attachment C – Financial Response and will be provided to the Contractor in order to complete and submit.  The proposed pricing on Attachment C – Financial Response will then be used in the Financial Evaluation.

findings.title: Pricing Requirements
findings.fact: All pricing offered on Attachment C must be equal to or better than the pricing offered for that SKU on the Contractor's Manufacturer Umbrella Contract.
findings.business_implication: Pricing on Attachment C cannot exceed the existing contract price, so bidders must ensure their offered prices are at or below the umbrella contract rates to remain competitive.
findings.action_recommendation: Review current Manufacturer Umbrella Contract pricing for all SKUs and set Attachment C pricing at or below those levels. Consider aggressive discounts to improve financial score.

quotes.quote: All pricing offered on Attachment C - Financial Response must be equal to or better than the pricing offered for that SKU on the Contractor's Manufacturer Umbrella Contract.

findings.title: Technical Evaluation of Mandatory Specifications
findings.fact: Only items with mandatory specifications are evaluated in the Technical Evaluation; additional items are reviewed only for inclusion in Lot 2 of the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract price list.
findings.business_implication: Technical evaluation focuses only on mandatory items, but additional items must still be on the price list to be included; otherwise they may be removed from the submission, potentially affecting configuration completeness.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure all additional items used to complete standard configurations are listed in Lot 2 of the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract price list. If any are missing, request contract modifications to add them before submission.

quotes.quote: Only items that have a mandatory specification will be evaluated in the Technical Evaluation; additional items needed to create the Standard Configuration listed in Section A of Attachment A- Technical Response will be reviewed only to determine if the items are included in Lot 2 of the Contractor’s Manufacturer Umbrella Contract price list.

findings.title: Required Products Discount Factored into Total Financial Score
findings.fact: The discount percentages bid on Required Products will be factored into the Total Financial Score.
findings.business_implication: The discount percentages on Required Products directly influence the financial evaluation, which is 100% of the total score. Aggressive discounts can significantly improve the bid's competitiveness and chances of winning.
findings.action_recommendation: Strategically set Required Product discount percentages to maximize the financial score while ensuring profitability. Analyze competitor pricing and margin thresholds to determine optimal discount levels.

quotes.quote: Contractors are encouraged to aggressively discount their pricing for their Required Products, as the pricing will be factored in the Total Financial Score.

findings.title: Pricing Requirements for Standard Configurations
findings.fact: Quoted pricing for Standard Configurations must not exceed the Net NYS Contract Price on the Manufacturer's Umbrella Contract.
findings.business_implication: Pricing for Standard Configurations is capped at the Net NYS Contract Price, limiting the bidder's ability to set higher prices. This ensures competitiveness but may compress margins.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure all quoted prices for Standard Configurations are at or below the Net NYS Contract Price. Review the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract price list to confirm compliance and identify opportunities for discounts to enhance competitiveness.

quotes.quote: In no event may quoted pricing exceed the Net NYS Contract Price on the Manufacturer’s Umbrella Contract.
In no event may quoted pricing exceed the Net NYS Contract Price on the Contractor’s Manufacturer Umbrella Contract.

findings.title: Discount Percentage Requirements for Required Products
findings.fact: Required Products discount percentages may be increased but not decreased during the term of the Agreement and any extensions.
findings.business_implication: Once bid, Required Product discount percentages cannot be lowered, locking in the bidder's pricing flexibility. This could impact profitability if costs rise or market conditions change.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully calculate the minimum viable discount percentages for Required Products, considering long-term cost structures and potential market fluctuations. Avoid overly aggressive discounts that may become unsustainable.

quotes.quote: The discount percentages may be increased, but not decreased during the term of any resulting Agreement and any extensions.
Required Product discount percentages may be increased, but not decreased during the term of any resulting Agreement and any extensions.

findings.title: Financial Evaluation Weighting
findings.fact: Financial Response is 100% of evaluation, with points allocated: Standard Configuration 50 points, Required Products (Warranty/Services 15, Components 30, Peripherals 5).
findings.business_implication: The financial proposal is the sole determinant of award, with Standard Configuration pricing carrying the most weight (50 points). Required Products collectively account for the other 50 points, with Components being the most significant among them.
findings.action_recommendation: Prioritize competitive pricing on Standard Configurations and Components, as they have the highest point values. Allocate pricing efforts to maximize scores in these areas while ensuring all required products are priced competitively.

quotes.quote: Financial Response : 100%  Total Financial Score is based on lowest cost and the points are weighted as follows: • Standard Configuration - 50 points • Required Products o Warranty/Services - 15 points o Components - 30 points o Peripherals - 5 points

findings.title: IDIQ Agreement with No Guaranteed Volume
findings.fact: The Agreement is an Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) award with no guarantee of volume or dollar value to be purchased.
findings.business_implication: There is no guaranteed revenue from this contract; actual purchases may vary significantly. This introduces uncertainty in revenue forecasting and may affect resource allocation.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess the potential upside and downside of the IDIQ structure. Prepare for variable demand by maintaining flexibility in supply chain and inventory. Consider the estimated $50 million aggregate value as a reference but do not rely on it as a guarantee.

quotes.quote: However, the Agreements resulting from this RFQ will be Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) awards.
There is no guarantee of volume to be purchased
There is no guarantee of dollar value to be purchased

findings.title: Agreement Term and Extension Options
findings.fact: The term of the Agreement is one year, with OGS having the right to extend for up to an additional one year, and a possible short-term extension of up to three months (or six months with contractor concurrence).
findings.business_implication: The contract duration is relatively short (1 year) but may be extended up to 2 years or more, providing potential for long-term revenue but also uncertainty. The unilateral extension right gives OGS leverage, and the short-term extension could lead to a gap in business if not renewed.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan for a possible multi-year engagement by preparing for extensions. Maintain flexibility in pricing and resources to accommodate potential extensions. Monitor contract end dates and proactively engage with OGS regarding renewal or extension discussions.

quotes.quote: The term of any resulting Agreement shall be one (1) year.
OGS reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to extend all or some Configurations of the Agreement for a period up to an additional one (1) year upon written notice to the Contractor.

In the event a replacement Agreement has not been issued, any Agreement let and awarded hereunder by the State, may be extended unilaterally by the State for an additional period of up to three (3) months upon notice to the Contractor with the same terms and conditions as the original Agreement including, but not limited to, prices and delivery requirements. With the concurrence of the Contractor, the extension may be for a period of up to six (6) months in lieu of three (3) months.

findings.title: Pricing Modification Procedures
findings.fact: Contractors can lower pricing at any time, add additional products (subject to approval), delete products under certain conditions, replace products, and update standard configurations, all through specified modification procedures.
findings.business_implication: This provides flexibility to adjust offerings in response to market changes, but also imposes administrative burden and requires adherence to strict procedures. It may also create opportunities to improve competitiveness by lowering prices or adding new products.
findings.action_recommendation: Establish a clear internal process for managing modifications, including timely submission of required forms and documentation. Monitor product lifecycles to proactively manage EOL and replacements. Ensure all modifications comply with OGS approval requirements to avoid delays or non-compliance.

quotes.quote: All Product pricing on the Contractor’s Agreement price list can be lowered at any time throughout the term of any resulting Agreement and any extensions.

After Agreement award, in order for a Product to be added to the Additional Products pricing category under the Agreement, a Product must first be approved on the Contractor’s Manufacturer Umbrella Contract in accordance with the Contractor’s Manufacturer Umbrella Contract Appendix C – Contract Modification Procedure.
Additional Products can only be removed from the Agreement if the Products are shown to OGS’ satisfaction to be incompatible with the Standard Configurations, unavailable, or at End of Life (EOL).

Replacements are defined as substitute Products which take the place of a previously awarded Product included in the Standard Configurations and/or Required Products, due to the awarded Product becoming incompatible with the Standard Configuration, unavailable or at Product EOL.

The Contractor will be able to update the entire Standard Configuration to a new model as long as acceptable proof that the Product has reached EOL or has become unavailable for purchase is provided in writing to the Agreement Contract Manager(s).

findings.title: Not-to-Exceed Pricing and Off-Contract Sales Prohibition
findings.fact: Agreement prices are Not-To-Exceed prices and off-contract sales are prohibited.
findings.business_implication: This ensures that the state gets the best possible pricing, but it also restricts the contractor's ability to offer lower prices outside the contract. It may limit flexibility in negotiating with individual customers and could impact profitability if costs rise.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that pricing is set competitively but sustainably, considering potential cost increases. Avoid any off-contract sales to prevent breach of contract. Monitor costs and consider requesting price adjustments if necessary, though the contract may not allow increases.

quotes.quote: Agreement prices are Not-To-Exceed prices. Off-Contract sales are prohibited.

findings.title: OGS Not Liable for Preparation Costs
findings.fact: OGS will not be held liable for any cost incurred by the Contractor for work performed in the preparation of a response to this RFQ.
findings.business_implication: The bidder bears all costs of preparing the proposal, which can be significant. There is no reimbursement if the bid is unsuccessful, so the bidder must carefully manage bid preparation costs.
findings.action_recommendation: Allocate resources efficiently and avoid excessive spending on proposal development. Consider the potential return on investment before committing extensive resources. Ensure that all internal stakeholders are aware of the non-reimbursable nature of bid costs.

quotes.quote: OGS will not be held liable for any cost incurred by the Contractor for work performed in the preparation of a response to this Request for Quote (RFQ).

findings.title: Contractor Assumes Risk for Timely Submission
findings.fact: Contractor assumes all risks for timely, properly submitted RFQ deliveries.
findings.business_implication: The bidder is responsible for ensuring that the proposal is submitted on time and in the correct format. Any delays or errors could result in rejection, leading to lost business opportunities.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement a robust submission process with internal checks and backups. Allow ample time for finalizing and submitting the proposal to avoid last-minute issues. Verify all submission requirements and confirm receipt with OGS.

quotes.quote: Contractor assumes all risks for timely, properly submitted RFQ deliveries.

findings.title: Contractor Must Furnish All Quantities Ordered
findings.fact: Contractor must furnish all quantities actually ordered by Authorized Users at or below the prices in the Agreement.
findings.business_implication: The contractor is obligated to supply any quantity ordered by authorized users at the agreed prices, regardless of the estimated volumes. This could lead to significant financial and operational strain if demand exceeds expectations, as the contractor must be prepared to meet potentially high order volumes without the ability to renegotiate prices.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure robust supply chain and inventory management to handle variable demand. Assess production capacity and subcontracting options to guarantee fulfillment of all orders. Consider including contingency plans for sudden spikes in orders.

quotes.quote: Contractor must furnish all quantities actually ordered by Authorized Users at or below the prices in the Aggregate Hardware Buy 23-01 Agreement.

findings.title: Contractor Responsible for Replacement of Incompatible Components
findings.fact: Replacement components must be compatible with Agreement peripherals or the Contractor will be responsible for replacement of both the component and the peripheral.
findings.business_implication: If a replacement component is incompatible with existing peripherals, the contractor bears the cost of replacing both the component and the peripheral. This could result in unexpected expenses and potential financial losses if compatibility issues arise.
findings.action_recommendation: Thoroughly test replacement components for compatibility with all peripherals listed in the agreement before offering them. Maintain a list of compatible components and peripherals. Establish a process for verifying compatibility and obtaining OGS approval before substitution.

quotes.quote: Replacement components must be compatible with Agreement peripherals or the Contractor will be responsible for replacement of both the component and the peripheral.

findings.title: Termination for Repeated Failure to Comply
findings.fact: OGS may terminate an Agreement under this RFQ, in whole or in part, for Contractor's repeated failure to comply with any requirement under the Agreement.
findings.business_implication: Repeated non-compliance with any agreement requirement can lead to termination of the entire agreement or parts of it. This poses a significant risk to the contractor's revenue stream and business relationship with OGS.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement strict compliance monitoring and internal controls to ensure all terms and conditions are met. Designate a compliance officer to oversee adherence to the agreement. Regularly audit processes to identify and rectify any potential non-compliance issues promptly.

quotes.quote: Terminate an Agreement under this RFQ, in whole or in part, for Contractor’s repeated failure to comply with any requirement under the Agreement.

findings.title: Termination for Delayed Deliveries
findings.fact: If OGS becomes aware of multiple incidents of delays in delivery, OGS reserves the right to enforce remedies including termination of the Agreement in whole or in part.
findings.business_implication: Multiple delivery delays could trigger termination of the agreement, leading to loss of business and potential financial penalties. This highlights the importance of reliable delivery performance.
findings.action_recommendation: Develop a robust logistics and delivery management system to ensure timely deliveries. Monitor delivery performance metrics and address any recurring issues proactively. Maintain open communication with OGS and authorized users to manage expectations and mitigate delays.

quotes.quote: If OGS becomes aware of multiple incidents of delays in delivery, OGS reserves the right to enforce any of the remedies available to us through the terms of this Agreement, including our rights to terminate the Agreement in whole or in part, and award to another contractor as per the terms of Section 7.22 Replacement Contractor.

findings.title: Termination for Failure to Submit Accurate Sales Reports
findings.fact: Failure to submit accurate sales reports on a timely basis may result in a responsibility hearing and possible termination of the Agreement in whole or in part.
findings.business_implication: Inaccurate or late sales reports can lead to a responsibility hearing and potential termination of the agreement. This could damage the contractor's reputation and result in loss of the contract.
findings.action_recommendation: Establish a robust sales reporting process with clear internal deadlines to ensure timely and accurate submissions. Assign dedicated personnel to prepare and review reports. Implement checks and balances to verify data accuracy before submission.

quotes.quote: Failure to submit accurate reports on a timely basis may result in a responsibility hearing, and possible termination of this Agreement in whole or in part, after which OGS reserves the right to award to another contractor as per the terms of Section 7.22 Replacement Contractor.

findings.title: Termination for Repeated Audit Errors
findings.fact: Repeated errors on subsequent fiscal audits may lead to termination of any resulting Agreement in whole or in part.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure high accuracy in sales reporting and fiscal audits to avoid termination of the agreement, which could result in loss of business and potential reputational damage.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement robust internal controls and verification processes for sales reporting, conduct regular internal audits, and ensure all submissions are accurate and timely to mitigate the risk of repeated errors.

quotes.quote: Repeated errors on subsequent audits may result in a responsibility hearing in relation to Contractor’s Manufacturer Umbrella Contract and may lead to termination of any resulting Agreement in whole or in part, after which OGS reserves the right to award to another contractor as per the terms of Section 7.22 Replacement Contractor.
